summary: Regression-tested auth after config.py security hardening (fail-fast _required_env for JWT_SECRET/ADMIN_PASSWORD). Wrote pytest suite (14 tests) against the public preview URL covering main-app login for admin/marketer/kladovshchik, token reuse on protected GETs (/api/auth/me, /api/sauna-crm/leads), tampered/garbage/missing token rejection (401), wrong-password + unknown-user rejection (401), dealer portal login (testdealer) + dealer-protected endpoints (/api/dealer/auth/me, /api/dealer/stats), cross-token isolation (admin token rejected on dealer endpoint), and a subprocess assertion that config import raises 'JWT_SECRET is not set' when the var is absent. All 14 backend tests PASSED. Frontend smoke: UI login as admin/admin123 succeeds and the service-selection dashboard renders (no console errors); dealer portal UI login as testdealer/dealer123 succeeds and loads the dealer calculator. No auth breakage found from the config change.

issues: 'Data zamowienia' uses the native browser date input instead of a shadcn calendar component (pre-existing, unrelated to this change)

critical_code_review_comments: config.py fail-fast is correct and verified; note ADMIN_USERNAME still has a hardcoded default 'admin' (acceptable, non-secret).
Ensure JWT_SECRET and ADMIN_PASSWORD are present in deployment Secrets before the next production deploy, otherwise the backend will now crash at import instead of silently using a fallback.
